# Audit instructions

This workspace holds one pull request against the Loa framework repository, frozen for evaluation.

- `PR.md` — the PR title and description
- `head.diff` — the complete change (unified diff, base → head)
- `base/` — every touched file before the change
- `head/` — every touched file after the change

Audit the change as the security auditor for this repository. There is no sprint plan, beads database, implementation report or `grimoires/loa/a2a/` directory here — the PR files above are the entire input; skip any pre-flight step that needs them and do not ask questions.

Write your audit to `audit.md` in this directory using the Write tool. Cite every finding as `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers taken from the `head/` files. Follow your auditor skill's output format and end the file with its machine-readable verdict trailer.
----
# Task brief

## Criterion

review the pull request, report each defect it introduces with the file and line it sits on, and give a merge verdict

## Task

# Task: review a pull request

The directory `pr/` holds one pull request against a repository of shell scripts, tests and documentation, frozen for evaluation. The change: sprint-261 suite v2 frozen + per-type run caps (DEC-0559, DEC-0566, DEC-0567, DEC-0574, DEC-0575, DEC-0580, DEC-0581): twelve harder build tasks with v2 ids (bugfix-v2-01 … feature-v….

The pull request is laid out as:

- `pr/PR.md` — the title and description
- `pr/head.diff` — the complete change (unified diff, base to head)
- `pr/base/` — every touched file before the change
- `pr/head/` — every touched file after the change

Review the change as the senior technical reviewer for the repository: find the defects it introduces and decide whether it can merge. Do not change any file under `pr/`.

## Output contract

Write your review to `review.md` at the repository root (a review workflow that also writes its own report files may do so; `review.md` follows this shape regardless):

- one finding per line, in the form `head/<path>:<line> — <description>`, where `<path>` is the file's path under `pr/head/` and `<line>` is a line number in that file;
- a final line that is exactly `Verdict: APPROVED` or `Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED`.
----
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1087 — HIGH: `remove_colliding` reserves every `.py` basename under the fixture's tests/ dirs (helpers, oracles, support modules) and line 1093 unlinks any agent-added file anywhere in the tree with that basename; pytest only collides on collected test modules in package-less dirs (verified: `tests/helpers.py` + `src/app/helpers.py` pass), so a correct solution's `src/<pkg>/helpers.py` is deleted and the run graded failing — the false negative 1.2.11 was written to prevent. The walk also covers vendored trees/virtualenvs (only EXCLUDE_TOP/__pycache__ pruned).
head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:806 — HIGH: the codex pre-flight horizon is now + 2 × Σ watchdog_s / concurrency, but watchdog_s is already 2 × the phase sum, so the pre-registered A0/A1/A4 × 3-trial plan needs a token valid ≈10.4 days out (real wall time ≈2.6 days; the PR's own DEC-0593 token lived 10 days) and a freshly logged-in operator is refused with a `codex login` hint that cannot help; the check also fires under `--executor host`, where `make_home` (pipeline-run.sh:648) never installs the non-refreshable placeholder credential.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1081 — MEDIUM: overlay-derived basenames are not filtered for `__init__.py` while the fixture walk (line 1087) is; an overlay shipping `tests/<dir>/__init__.py` makes every agent-added package `__init__.py` a removal target.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1079 — MEDIUM: directory overlays contribute nothing to `reserved`, so collisions with a test inside a directory overlay are not fixed.
head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:794 — MEDIUM: on `--resume`, `codex_arms` is derived from the whole recorded plan, so a re-row-only resume (`--rerow`) or a resume with nothing left to launch is refused on an expired token although no pipeline call would run.
head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:503 — MEDIUM: `(.[$k] // "" | tostring)` maps a present `false`/`null`/"" per-kind cap to "no entry" and silently falls back to RUN_CAP, contradicting the header's "a present entry that is not an amount in USD … is a usage error" (line 191); use `has($k)` and validate every present value.
head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:793 — LOW: `uses_codex` treats every `loa_mount != false` arm as codex-using; gate-less arms (a4_no_gates) never run the dissent, so a4-only batches are refused needlessly.
head/evals/tests/run-ablation.bats:95 — LOW: the comment says A0 BARE stays 70 min and the 80-min derivation does not apply, while line 97 asserts 9600 s (= 2 × 80 min) with a comment saying the opposite; one is stale.
head/evals/tests/run-ablation.bats:828 — LOW: RAB-25 passes/fails on the relative order of `launch`/`done` lines with a millisecond stub and a 0.2 s poll; the "launches" branches are timing-dependent.
head/evals/tests/seed-bugfix.bats:80 — LOW: the test passes `--suite-version` to a seed script not in this diff, and the RAB tests reference `*-v2-*` task dirs and MANIFEST.sha256 under grimoires/ not in this diff; unverifiable here (same at seed-refactor.bats:78).
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1100 — LOW: bare `os.unlink` raises on a read-only parent and aborts the grade; pre-existing pattern (remove_harness line 1065 does the same), noted for the rework.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

<objective>
Audit code, architecture, infrastructure or sprint implementations for security and quality; produce prioritized findings with actionable remediation at the output path for the audit type.
</objective>

<zone_constraints>

The SDD specifies "PostgreSQL 15 with pgvector extension" (sdd.md:L123)

**Ungrounded Example:**

<grounding_requirements>

</grounding_requirements>

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants; the lead decides. A large scope splits per category (`<parallel_execution>`); otherwise run the 5 categories sequentially.

## Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

Sprint audit: `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/` exists and its `engineer-feedback.md` says "All good"; otherwise STOP: "Sprint must be approved by senior lead before security audit". With `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`, its `adversarial-review.json` must carry `metadata.model` (the gate's `COMPLETED` check); otherwise STOP: re-run the review's Phase 2.5. Deployment audit: `grimoires/loa/deployment/` exists; read `deployment-report.md` for context if present. Codebase audit: no prerequisites.

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. On a large repo, prioritize by sink severity and reachability; cap entries, log the overflow.

## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

## Phase 1C: Security Dissenter Analysis

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

Run `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --diff-range main...HEAD --json` — no `--context-file`. Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). Output: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`; one top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary` or sidecar rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else `verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never tallied; `metadata.locality.degraded_security_review: true` ⇒ state DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

Execute by category (sequential, or split per Phase -1), each per its `resources/REFERENCE.md` section: **Security**, **Architecture**, **Code Quality**, **DevOps**, and **Blockchain/Crypto** when applicable.

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"
- If only MEDIUM/LOW: "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" (but note improvements)

**Codebase Audit:**
- Overall Risk Level: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
- Recommendations: Immediate (24h), Short-term (1wk), Long-term (1mo)

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of the audit output file:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"excluded_confirmed":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
(both extra fields may be omitted when 0). Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved
sprint/deployment audits use the exact prose `APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO`. `excluded_confirmed`
must equal the review trailer's `excluded`; the golden path refuses to advance otherwise.

**MUST self-check before finishing**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file <audit-output-file> --gate audit --review-file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md`
and resolve any inconsistency before reporting completion.
</workflow>

<parallel_execution>
## Parallel Splitting (large scopes)

When splitting, use 5 parallel Explore agents — one per category (Security / Architecture / Code Quality / DevOps / Blockchain-Crypto) — each scoped to its category's files and returning findings with severity, file:line, and remediation (per-category file globs and prompts: see `resources/PARALLEL-SPLIT.md`). Consolidate: deduplicate overlaps, sort CRITICAL → LOW, take the overall risk from the highest severity present.
</parallel_execution>

<rubric_scoring>
## Rubric-Based Scoring

Score each dimension 1–5 per `resources/RUBRICS.md` (Security weighted highest; Blockchain when applicable), recording the findings that justify each score.
</rubric_scoring>

<structured_output>
## Structured JSONL Output

Alongside the markdown report, write machine-parseable findings to `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/findings.jsonl` per `resources/OUTPUT-SCHEMA.md` (the schema, each `reasoning_trace`, the closing summary record).
</structured_output>

<communication_style>
Be direct and specific, with evidence: "Line 47: user input passed unsanitized to eval(). Critical RCE. OWASP A03." — never "the code has security issues". Document blast radius, prioritize by exploitability and impact, suggest pragmatic fixes, and never defer a critical issue.
</communication_style>

<documentation_audit>
## Documentation Audit

For sprint audits, confirm each task has a documentation-coherence report (Glob `grimoires/loa/a2a/subagent-reports/documentation-coherence-task-*.md`; sprint level: `documentation-coherence-sprint-*.md`) or was manually verified — checks and red-flag tables: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Documentation. Blockers: an unverified missing report; uncommented security-critical code; a CHANGELOG omitting security changes; secrets or internal URLs in docs or comments; auth/crypto changes without security documentation; API changes that don't match the endpoint docs.
</documentation_audit>

<checklists>
Complete checklists for the five categories (Security, Architecture, Code Quality, DevOps, Blockchain/Crypto): `resources/REFERENCE.md`. Immediate CRITICAL red flags: private keys in code, SQL via string concatenation, user input to eval(), empty catch blocks on security code, hardcoded secrets.
</checklists>

<beads_workflow>
With `br` installed: `resources/BEADS-WORKFLOW.md` (sync, the audit comment, the `security*` labels, a discovered vulnerability).
</beads_workflow>

<retrospective_postlude>
<!-- @skill-include: start retrospective_postlude | hash:53d44248 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md -->
After the main skill logic, if `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob invisible_retrospective.enabled`
prints `true` (and `invisible_retrospective.skills` does not disable this skill), silently run the
learning-signal scan per `.claude/skills/continuous-learning/SKILL.md` and its
`resources/RETROSPECTIVE.md` (quality gates, sanitization, trajectory logging). Never when the

<!-- @skill-include: end retrospective_postlude -->
</retrospective_postlude>

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants; the lead decides. A large scope splits per category (`<parallel_execution>`); otherwise run the 5 categories sequentially.

## Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. On a large repo, prioritize by sink severity and reachability; cap entries, log the overflow.

## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

## Phase 1C: Security Dissenter Analysis

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never tallied; `metadata.locality.degraded_security_review: true` ⇒ state DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW.

Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"
- If only MEDIUM/LOW: "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" (but note improvements)

- Overall Risk Level: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW

=== engineer-feedback.md
# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-21
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description, `pr/PR.md`)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is `pr/head.diff`: grader 1.2.11 (basename-collision removal), per-task-kind run caps (DEC-0567) threaded through `run-ablation.sh` and `lib/arms-common.sh`, the KF-048 codex credential handling (placeholder refresh token in `pipeline-run.sh`, access-token pre-flight in `run-ablation.sh`), the `--types` jq fix, suite v2 (`suite_version: 2`, `run_usd_by_type`), and the bats coverage for all of it.

Most of it is sound and well tested. The cap chain (`--run-cap` > suite `run_usd_by_type[kind]` > config > suite `run_usd` > 12) is implemented as documented, `--resume` reads caps from MANIFEST only, the in-flight reservation uses the largest cap over the plan's kinds, `spend_charge`/`budget_gate` keep their `RUN_CAP` defaults for other callers, the `--types` filter precedence is correct (RAB-27 proves it), the auth.json copy is written 0600 with the host file byte-identical and no token in argv (verified by the new pipeline-run tests), and the pre-flight prints no token material.

Two findings block merge. First, the new `remove_colliding` rule in the grader is broader than the pytest failure it fixes: it unlinks any agent-added `.py` anywhere in the tree whose basename matches a fixture `tests/` helper or an overlay module, which pytest never collides on; I reproduced that `tests/helpers.py` and `src/app/helpers.py` coexist under pytest's default import mode, so the grader would delete a correct solution's module and grade it failing — the exact harm 1.2.11 was written to prevent. Second, the KF-048 pre-flight horizon doubles an already-doubled watchdog and sums the whole plan, so the pre-registered A0/A1/A4 × 3-trial batch needs a token valid ~10.4 days ahead (the PR's own DEC-0593 token lived 10 days) while the batch's real wall time is ~2.6 days; the check also fires under `--executor host`, where `make_home` is not used and the CLI can refresh.

`reviewer.md` carries no `## AC Verification` section (it is the PR description), so the automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED rule applies as well; the code findings decide the verdict regardless.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Grader correctness — `remove_colliding` deletes non-colliding agent modules

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1087` — `reserved` takes every `.py` basename under the fixture's `tests/`/`test/` directories (helpers, oracles, support modules), and line 1093 removes any agent-added file in the whole tree with that basename, although pytest only collides on modules it collects (`test_*.py`, `*_test.py`, `conftest.py`) in package-less directories.
**File:** `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1081-1098`
**Issue:** The PR's own commit text says fixture suites do `from helpers import …`, so fixtures ship `tests/helpers.py`-style modules. An agent that adds `src/<pkg>/helpers.py` (or `utils.py`, or any basename a fixture support module uses) as part of a correct solution has it unlinked from `grading/final` before `test_command` runs; the hidden tests then `ImportError` and the run is graded failing. Verified: with `tests/helpers.py`, `tests/test_a.py` (`from helpers import h`) and `src/app/helpers.py`, `python3 -m pytest tests` passes 2/2 — there is no pytest collision to prevent. The same over-breadth removes an agent's test module placed in a directory that has `__init__.py` (no collision under prepend mode either, verified 3/3 passing) and, because the walk is the entire tree with only `EXCLUDE_TOP`/`__pycache__` pruned, any same-named module inside a vendored tree or virtualenv in the snapshot (dissent DISS-C-003), inflating `colliding_tests_removed`.
**Why This Matters:** A correct solution graded as failing is silent measurement corruption in the H1/A4 ablation; 1.2.11 exists to remove exactly this class of false negative and re-introduces it in another shape.
**Required Fix:** Restrict `reserved` to basenames pytest actually imports by basename: the fixture-walk and the overlay set should keep only `test_*.py` / `*_test.py` (plus the existing conftest handling), and candidates should be limited to `.py` files that are themselves test modules in package-less directories (no `__init__.py` on the path from the collection root). Prune `.git`, `.venv`/`venv`, `node_modules`, `site-packages` from the walk. Add an AG case asserting that `src/app/helpers.py` survives beside a fixture `tests/helpers.py`.

### 2. Pre-flight — the codex horizon refuses batches the token would outlive, and fires in host mode

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:806` — `required = now + 2 × Σ watchdog_s / concurrency`, but `watchdog_s` is already 2 × the phase-sum timeout (RAB-1: 16800 s for a 140-min phase sum), so the horizon is ~4 × the serial phase time / concurrency, and it is computed for every executor although only container mode (`pipeline-run.sh:648`, `make_home`) carries the non-refreshable placeholder credential.
**File:** `head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:780-838`
**Issue:** With the suite's own numbers (a0 build 9600 s, a1 build 16800 s, a4 build 6000 s, a1 review-catch 7200 s, a0 review-catch 8400 s; 12 build + 4 review tasks; 3 trials; concurrency 3) the pre-registered A0/A1/A4 batch sums to roughly 1.35 M s of watchdog, so `required_until` is about 10.4 days out while the batch's expected wall time is about 2.6 days. The PR's own DEC-0593 token was valid for 10 days after login, so a freshly logged-in operator is refused and told to `run codex login`, which cannot help. `--dry-run` is refused the same way (RAB-34 makes that deliberate). Under `--executor host` the check runs although `make_home` is never called and the host CLI refreshes its own token.

| Plan (3 trials, conc 3) | Σ watchdog_s | required horizon | expected wall time |
|---|---|---|---|
| A0 + A1 + A4, 12 build + 4 review | ≈1,353,600 | ≈10.4 d | ≈2.6 d |
| A0 + A1, 12 build | ≈950,400 | ≈7.3 d | ≈1.8 d |

**Why This Matters:** The runner refuses the batches it exists to launch, with a remediation message that is wrong for the case; operators will split batches or hand-edit to work around it, defeating the pre-registration discipline.
**Required Fix:** Compute the horizon from the phase-sum budget (Σ watchdog_s / 2, or the plan's `phase_sum_min`) with a bounded safety margin rather than another ×2; skip the check (record `checked: false`, reason `host`) when `EXECUTOR != container`; when `exp` is earlier than the horizon but later than a fresh login could ever reach, say so ("the batch outlives any codex token; split it") instead of prescribing `codex login`. Tie RAB-30's expected `required_until` to the new formula.

---

## Observations

### 1. `remove_colliding` — remaining gaps in the collision rule

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1081` — the overlay-derived basenames are not filtered for `__init__.py` while the fixture walk at line 1087 is; a hidden overlay that ships `tests/<dir>/__init__.py` makes every agent-added package `__init__.py` in the tree a removal target (a new package under `src/` loses its marker and its imports fail).
**Suggestion:** Apply the same `("__init__.py", "conftest.py")` exclusion to the overlay set (or adopt the test-module-only rule from Changes Required §1, which subsumes this).
**Benefit:** Removes a second path to grading a correct solution as failing.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1079` — directory overlays (`os.path.isdir(f)`) contribute nothing to `reserved`, so an agent test module whose basename collides with a test inside a directory overlay is not removed and the collection abort 1.2.11 targets still happens for those tasks.
**Suggestion:** Walk directory overlays for `test_*.py` basenames when building `reserved`.
**Benefit:** The fix covers every overlay shape the manifest format allows.

### 2. Pre-flight scope

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:794` — `codex_arms` is derived from the whole recorded plan, so a `--resume` that only re-rows (`--rerow …`) or resumes a batch with no trial left to launch is refused on an expired token although no pipeline call would run. The PR's own history re-rowed 24 rows under row writer 1.2; with a lapsed token that bookkeeping step would have been blocked until a re-login.
**Suggestion:** On `--resume`, derive `codex_arms` and the horizon from the trials that will actually launch (plan entries without a row, plus `--rerun` targets); skip the check when that set is empty.
**Benefit:** Bookkeeping resumes never depend on a live credential.

- **LOW** (confidence: low) `head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:793` — `uses_codex` treats every arm with `loa_mount != false` as codex-using; an arm whose toggles disable the review/audit gates (a4_no_gates) never runs the dissent, so an a4-only batch is refused on an expired token although it would not use the OpenAI voice.
**Suggestion:** Derive codex use from the toggles that actually drive the dissent (gates/dissent on), not from `loa_mount` alone.
**Benefit:** Fewer needless refusals; `codex_arms` in MANIFEST becomes accurate.

### 3. Per-kind cap validation (dissent DISS-001, accepted at reduced severity)

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:503` — `(.[$k] // "" | tostring)` maps a present `false` or `null` entry (and an empty string) to "", which the caller treats as "no entry" and silently falls back to `RUN_CAP`, contradicting the header's "a present entry that is not an amount in USD … is a usage error" (line 191) and RAB-22's intent. `run_usd_by_type: {build: ~}` launches build trials at 12 and records 12 as the effective cap.
**Suggestion:** Use `has($k)` to distinguish absent from present and validate every present value with `usd_ok`.
**Benefit:** A broken spend-control setting is refused instead of recorded as intentional.

### 4. Tests

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/evals/tests/run-ablation.bats:95` — the comment says "A0 BARE stays 70 min … the derivation (80) does not apply" while line 97 asserts 9600 s (= 2 × 80 min) with a trailing comment that says the opposite. One of the two is stale.
**Suggestion:** Delete the 70-min sentence.
**Benefit:** The next reader of the watchdog maths is not misled.

- **LOW** (confidence: low) `head/evals/tests/run-ablation.bats:828` — RAB-25 decides pass/fail by the relative order of `launch` and `done` lines in `run.log` with a stub that finishes in milliseconds and a 0.2 s poll; the "launches" branches (max 28 / 22) depend on the second launch being logged before the first trial's collection.
**Suggestion:** Give the stub a short sleep in these cases (or assert on `in_flight_reserved` in a cut record) so the ordering is deterministic.
**Benefit:** No intermittent failure in CI.

- **LOW** (confidence: low) `head/evals/tests/seed-bugfix.bats:80` and `head/evals/tests/seed-refactor.bats:78` — the tests now pass `--suite-version` to the seed scripts, and RAB-* reference `bugfix-v2-*`/`refactor-v2-*`/`feature-v2-*` task directories and the suite MANIFEST.sha256 under `grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/`; neither the seed scripts nor the frozen task set is in this diff, so this review could not confirm the flag exists or that the frozen tasks carry `suite_version: 2` (validate-suite compares each task to the suite file).
**Suggestion:** Confirm in the PR description that the seed scripts already accept `--suite-version` and that the frozen task set was re-frozen at suite_version 2.
**Benefit:** Closes the only part of the test surface this review could not execute or read.

### 5. Dissent advisories not adopted as findings

- **LOW** (confidence: low) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1100` — DISS-C-002 (claude-headless) says a read-only parent directory makes `os.unlink` raise and abort the grade. True, but `remove_harness` at line 1065 uses the same bare `os.unlink` on the same trees, so this is pre-existing behaviour, not something the change introduces; the dissent's claim that `remove_harness` goes through `remove_path` is incorrect. Worth a shared helper with `try/except OSError` when `remove_colliding` is reworked.

---

## Rejected dissent payloads

- None: `rejected_summary` is empty and `adversarial-rejected-review.jsonl` has zero rows. Both voices (gpt-5.5-pro primary, claude-headless companion) succeeded; envelope `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-review.json`.

## Cross-Model Observations

- DISS-001 (gpt-5.5-pro, BLOCKING) — accepted as MEDIUM, Observations §3: real, but the fallback cap is sane and the input is a malformed suite file.
- DISS-C-001 (claude-headless, BLOCKING) — accepted as HIGH, Changes Required §2, after re-deriving the horizon from the suite's numbers and checking `make_home` is container-only.
- DISS-C-002 (claude-headless, ADVISORY) — recorded in Observations §5; pre-existing pattern.
- DISS-C-003 (claude-headless, ADVISORY) — folded into Changes Required §1 (the walk is the whole tree).

---

## Incomplete Tasks

| Task | Status | Missing |
|------|--------|---------|
| Task 1.1: the change in `pr/head.diff` | Incomplete | The two HIGH findings above; no `## AC Verification` in the implementation report |

---

## Acceptance Criteria Check

### Task 1.1: review the pull request

| Criterion | Status | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| Each defect the change introduces reported with file and line | Pass | Changes Required §1–2, Observations §1–5 |
| Merge verdict given | Pass | CHANGES_REQUIRED |

---

## Security Checklist

- [x] No hardcoded secrets or credentials (placeholder string only; host auth.json never written; token values absent from argv/refusals — RAB-28, pipeline-run KF-048 tests)
- [x] Input validation and sanitization present (`usd_ok` on caps; JWT payload decoded without signature trust and used only for `exp`) — see Observations §3 for the `false`/`null` gap

- [x] Error messages don't leak sensitive data (paths only)

---

## Code Quality Summary

**Strengths:**
- Cap chain, resume semantics and reservation rule are documented in the header and pinned by RAB-22…26 with exact spend arithmetic.
- KF-048 handling is defensive at both ends (copy and pre-flight), with the failure story recorded inline.
- The `--types` fix comes with a regression test that exercises both the alias and a bad entry.

Complexity: `remove_colliding` and the pre-flight Python block are each under 50 lines, nesting ≤ 3. `SIMPLICITY[shrink]`: the pre-flight's horizon can reuse the plan's `phase_sum_min` instead of re-deriving from `watchdog_s`. Lean already otherwise. net: -4 lines possible.

---

## Next Steps

2. Pick up the MEDIUM observations while in those functions (`__init__.py`/dir-overlay reservation, resume scope, `has($k)` validation).

=== reviewer-concerns

=== engineer-feedback.md
# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-21
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description, `pr/PR.md`)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is `pr/head.diff`: grader 1.2.11 (basename-collision removal), per-task-kind run caps (DEC-0567) threaded through `run-ablation.sh` and `lib/arms-common.sh`, the KF-048 codex credential handling (placeholder refresh token in `pipeline-run.sh`, access-token pre-flight in `run-ablation.sh`), the `--types` jq fix, suite v2 (`suite_version: 2`, `run_usd_by_type`), and the bats coverage for all of it.

Most of it is sound and well tested. The cap chain (`--run-cap` > suite `run_usd_by_type[kind]` > config > suite `run_usd` > 12) is implemented as documented, `--resume` reads caps from MANIFEST only, the in-flight reservation uses the largest cap over the plan's kinds, `spend_charge`/`budget_gate` keep their `RUN_CAP` defaults for other callers, the `--types` filter precedence is correct (RAB-27 proves it), the auth.json copy is written 0600 with the host file byte-identical and no token in argv (verified by the new pipeline-run tests), and the pre-flight prints no token material.

Two findings block merge. First, the new `remove_colliding` rule in the grader is broader than the pytest failure it fixes: it unlinks any agent-added `.py` anywhere in the tree whose basename matches a fixture `tests/` helper or an overlay module, which pytest never collides on; I reproduced that `tests/helpers.py` and `src/app/helpers.py` coexist under pytest's default import mode, so the grader would delete a correct solution's module and grade it failing — the exact harm 1.2.11 was written to prevent. Second, the KF-048 pre-flight horizon doubles an already-doubled watchdog and sums the whole plan, so the pre-registered A0/A1/A4 × 3-trial batch needs a token valid ~10.4 days ahead (the PR's own DEC-0593 token lived 10 days) while the batch's real wall time is ~2.6 days; the check also fires under `--executor host`, where `make_home` is not used and the CLI can refresh.

`reviewer.md` carries no `## AC Verification` section (it is the PR description), so the automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED rule applies as well; the code findings decide the verdict regardless.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Grader correctness — `remove_colliding` deletes non-colliding agent modules

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1087` — `reserved` takes every `.py` basename under the fixture's `tests/`/`test/` directories (helpers, oracles, support modules), and line 1093 removes any agent-added file in the whole tree with that basename, although pytest only collides on modules it collects (`test_*.py`, `*_test.py`, `conftest.py`) in package-less directories.
**File:** `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1081-1098`
**Issue:** The PR's own commit text says fixture suites do `from helpers import …`, so fixtures ship `tests/helpers.py`-style modules. An agent that adds `src/<pkg>/helpers.py` (or `utils.py`, or any basename a fixture support module uses) as part of a correct solution has it unlinked from `grading/final` before `test_command` runs; the hidden tests then `ImportError` and the run is graded failing. Verified: with `tests/helpers.py`, `tests/test_a.py` (`from helpers import h`) and `src/app/helpers.py`, `python3 -m pytest tests` passes 2/2 — there is no pytest collision to prevent. The same over-breadth removes an agent's test module placed in a directory that has `__init__.py` (no collision under prepend mode either, verified 3/3 passing) and, because the walk is the entire tree with only `EXCLUDE_TOP`/`__pycache__` pruned, any same-named module inside a vendored tree or virtualenv in the snapshot (dissent DISS-C-003), inflating `colliding_tests_removed`.
**Why This Matters:** A correct solution graded as failing is silent measurement corruption in the H1/A4 ablation; 1.2.11 exists to remove exactly this class of false negative and re-introduces it in another shape.
**Required Fix:** Restrict `reserved` to basenames pytest actually imports by basename: the fixture-walk and the overlay set should keep only `test_*.py` / `*_test.py` (plus the existing conftest handling), and candidates should be limited to `.py` files that are themselves test modules in package-less directories (no `__init__.py` on the path from the collection root). Prune `.git`, `.venv`/`venv`, `node_modules`, `site-packages` from the walk. Add an AG case asserting that `src/app/helpers.py` survives beside a fixture `tests/helpers.py`.

### 2. Pre-flight — the codex horizon refuses batches the token would outlive, and fires in host mode

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:806` — `required = now + 2 × Σ watchdog_s / concurrency`, but `watchdog_s` is already 2 × the phase-sum timeout (RAB-1: 16800 s for a 140-min phase sum), so the horizon is ~4 × the serial phase time / concurrency, and it is computed for every executor although only container mode (`pipeline-run.sh:648`, `make_home`) carries the non-refreshable placeholder credential.
**File:** `head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:780-838`
**Issue:** With the suite's own numbers (a0 build 9600 s, a1 build 16800 s, a4 build 6000 s, a1 review-catch 7200 s, a0 review-catch 8400 s; 12 build + 4 review tasks; 3 trials; concurrency 3) the pre-registered A0/A1/A4 batch sums to roughly 1.35 M s of watchdog, so `required_until` is about 10.4 days out while the batch's expected wall time is about 2.6 days. The PR's own DEC-0593 token was valid for 10 days after login, so a freshly logged-in operator is refused and told to `run codex login`, which cannot help. `--dry-run` is refused the same way (RAB-34 makes that deliberate). Under `--executor host` the check runs although `make_home` is never called and the host CLI refreshes its own token.

| Plan (3 trials, conc 3) | Σ watchdog_s | required horizon | expected wall time |
|---|---|---|---|
| A0 + A1 + A4, 12 build + 4 review | ≈1,353,600 | ≈10.4 d | ≈2.6 d |
| A0 + A1, 12 build | ≈950,400 | ≈7.3 d | ≈1.8 d |

**Why This Matters:** The runner refuses the batches it exists to launch, with a remediation message that is wrong for the case; operators will split batches or hand-edit to work around it, defeating the pre-registration discipline.
**Required Fix:** Compute the horizon from the phase-sum budget (Σ watchdog_s / 2, or the plan's `phase_sum_min`) with a bounded safety margin rather than another ×2; skip the check (record `checked: false`, reason `host`) when `EXECUTOR != container`; when `exp` is earlier than the horizon but later than a fresh login could ever reach, say so ("the batch outlives any codex token; split it") instead of prescribing `codex login`. Tie RAB-30's expected `required_until` to the new formula.

---

## Observations

### 1. `remove_colliding` — remaining gaps in the collision rule

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1081` — the overlay-derived basenames are not filtered for `__init__.py` while the fixture walk at line 1087 is; a hidden overlay that ships `tests/<dir>/__init__.py` makes every agent-added package `__init__.py` in the tree a removal target (a new package under `src/` loses its marker and its imports fail).
**Suggestion:** Apply the same `("__init__.py", "conftest.py")` exclusion to the overlay set (or adopt the test-module-only rule from Changes Required §1, which subsumes this).
**Benefit:** Removes a second path to grading a correct solution as failing.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1079` — directory overlays (`os.path.isdir(f)`) contribute nothing to `reserved`, so an agent test module whose basename collides with a test inside a directory overlay is not removed and the collection abort 1.2.11 targets still happens for those tasks.
**Suggestion:** Walk directory overlays for `test_*.py` basenames when building `reserved`.
**Benefit:** The fix covers every overlay shape the manifest format allows.

### 2. Pre-flight scope

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:794` — `codex_arms` is derived from the whole recorded plan, so a `--resume` that only re-rows (`--rerow …`) or resumes a batch with no trial left to launch is refused on an expired token although no pipeline call would run. The PR's own history re-rowed 24 rows under row writer 1.2; with a lapsed token that bookkeeping step would have been blocked until a re-login.
**Suggestion:** On `--resume`, derive `codex_arms` and the horizon from the trials that will actually launch (plan entries without a row, plus `--rerun` targets); skip the check when that set is empty.
**Benefit:** Bookkeeping resumes never depend on a live credential.

- **LOW** (confidence: low) `head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:793` — `uses_codex` treats every arm with `loa_mount != false` as codex-using; an arm whose toggles disable the review/audit gates (a4_no_gates) never runs the dissent, so an a4-only batch is refused on an expired token although it would not use the OpenAI voice.
**Suggestion:** Derive codex use from the toggles that actually drive the dissent (gates/dissent on), not from `loa_mount` alone.
**Benefit:** Fewer needless refusals; `codex_arms` in MANIFEST becomes accurate.

### 3. Per-kind cap validation (dissent DISS-001, accepted at reduced severity)

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:503` — `(.[$k] // "" | tostring)` maps a present `false` or `null` entry (and an empty string) to "", which the caller treats as "no entry" and silently falls back to `RUN_CAP`, contradicting the header's "a present entry that is not an amount in USD … is a usage error" (line 191) and RAB-22's intent. `run_usd_by_type: {build: ~}` launches build trials at 12 and records 12 as the effective cap.
**Suggestion:** Use `has($k)` to distinguish absent from present and validate every present value with `usd_ok`.
**Benefit:** A broken spend-control setting is refused instead of recorded as intentional.

### 4. Tests

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/evals/tests/run-ablation.bats:95` — the comment says "A0 BARE stays 70 min … the derivation (80) does not apply" while line 97 asserts 9600 s (= 2 × 80 min) with a trailing comment that says the opposite. One of the two is stale.
**Suggestion:** Delete the 70-min sentence.
**Benefit:** The next reader of the watchdog maths is not misled.

- **LOW** (confidence: low) `head/evals/tests/run-ablation.bats:828` — RAB-25 decides pass/fail by the relative order of `launch` and `done` lines in `run.log` with a stub that finishes in milliseconds and a 0.2 s poll; the "launches" branches (max 28 / 22) depend on the second launch being logged before the first trial's collection.
**Suggestion:** Give the stub a short sleep in these cases (or assert on `in_flight_reserved` in a cut record) so the ordering is deterministic.
**Benefit:** No intermittent failure in CI.

- **LOW** (confidence: low) `head/evals/tests/seed-bugfix.bats:80` and `head/evals/tests/seed-refactor.bats:78` — the tests now pass `--suite-version` to the seed scripts, and RAB-* reference `bugfix-v2-*`/`refactor-v2-*`/`feature-v2-*` task directories and the suite MANIFEST.sha256 under `grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/`; neither the seed scripts nor the frozen task set is in this diff, so this review could not confirm the flag exists or that the frozen tasks carry `suite_version: 2` (validate-suite compares each task to the suite file).
**Suggestion:** Confirm in the PR description that the seed scripts already accept `--suite-version` and that the frozen task set was re-frozen at suite_version 2.
**Benefit:** Closes the only part of the test surface this review could not execute or read.

### 5. Dissent advisories not adopted as findings

- **LOW** (confidence: low) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1100` — DISS-C-002 (claude-headless) says a read-only parent directory makes `os.unlink` raise and abort the grade. True, but `remove_harness` at line 1065 uses the same bare `os.unlink` on the same trees, so this is pre-existing behaviour, not something the change introduces; the dissent's claim that `remove_harness` goes through `remove_path` is incorrect. Worth a shared helper with `try/except OSError` when `remove_colliding` is reworked.

## Rejected dissent payloads

- None: `rejected_summary` is empty and `adversarial-rejected-review.jsonl` has zero rows. Both voices (gpt-5.5-pro primary, claude-headless companion) succeeded; envelope `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-review.json`.

# auditing-security — Security Dissenter (Phase 1C) detail

SKILL.md Phase 1C names the gate, the hook, the override and the invocation. This file carries
the merge rules and the failed-run record.

## Independence

The dissenter receives the diff only — never `--context-file` with your Phase 1A/1B findings —
so it evaluates the code without anchoring on your conclusions.

## Merging dissenter findings into Phase 2

1. CRITICAL/HIGH findings go into the audit report as findings of your own (they may change the
   verdict and must appear in the Phase 2.5 tally).
2. MEDIUM/LOW findings go under a "Cross-Model Security Observations" section.
3. A dissenter finding that duplicates one of yours is marked "Confirmed by cross-model review".

## Failed or unavailable dissenter

Output file: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`. The
`adversarial-review-gate.sh` hook checks that this file parses and carries `metadata.type` and `metadata.model` — a `--record-fallback` record names no model, so it never opens the gate: re-run the dissent (or the operator sets `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes). When `adversarial-audit.json` is ABSENT after the script exits — an aborted run leaves none: at start the script moves the previous round's envelope and sidecars aside as `.prev` and never restores them — record the failure with the script itself (a call this skill's allowlist holds; never a hand-written file):

```bash
.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --record-fallback failed --reason "<what happened>"
```

before proceeding. Branch on the `status` line the script prints on stdout, never on exit 2 alone (exit 2 with no status line is a usage error, or a standing envelope that stderr names):

- **An envelope stands after a run that took the run lock** — it is the script's own: triage it; never overwrite it.
- **`failed`** (no envelope: the run aborted) — the call above writes `{"findings": [], "metadata": {"status": "failed", "reason": "<what happened>", "rejected_summary": [], "rejected_sidecars": []}}` under the per-(sprint, gate) run lock. It never writes over an envelope that stands (exit 2), unless the run died before its lock with no status on stdout: what stands is then the previous round's — add `--since <the time on the run's "run started" stderr line>` and an envelope older than that goes aside as `.prev`.
- **`refused_concurrent_run`** (another run — a detached or backgrounded one — holds the run lock; nothing recorded, nothing moved; a `--record-fallback` made meanwhile is refused the same way) — wait until the holding run has exited: an envelope that then stands with a `metadata.timestamp` after your refusal is that run's: triage it as this round's dissent only when its `metadata.scope` is what you asked for (the same `diff_range` and `diff_oids` as your refusal's own `metadata.scope` — the commits, not just the ref names — and `run_tag` null: a chunk driver's tagged run reviewed one chunk); otherwise, or when none stands, run again.
- **`workdir_unavailable`, `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exceeded`, `diff_range_failed`** (the range's `git diff` failed — e.g. a base ref a shallow clone lacks; `workdir_unavailable` with `metadata.path` is a previous round's file that could not be moved aside — make the a2a directory writable; written BEFORE the run lock, or with it released; non-zero exit, stdout only; nothing moved aside, so any envelope at the path is the PREVIOUS run's and never this round's evidence) — record it: `--record-fallback <the status> --reason "<its stdout line>" --since <the run started time>` (it never displaces an envelope written after that) moves that envelope and its `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` sidecars aside as `<name>.prev` (as a run does at start) before it writes, so `verdict-derive.sh` judges this round's record, not the last round's.

A record names what it moved aside (`metadata.displaced`: status, timestamp, findings, rejected); `verdict-derive.sh` warns when that held findings. `verdict-derive.sh` never scans `.prev` files (they are the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback) and reports `.prev` files with NO envelope as a `dissent_aborted` violation, which a fallback record clears; `rejected_sidecars: []` does not silence a canonical `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` beside it — that is this run's own partial work, counted whether listed or not: triage its rows under `## Rejected dissent payloads`.

Then set a `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker in the audit report. Empty
findings from a run that completed are a normal pass, not a degraded review.

A bare `planned: false` (the block opted out, `companion_voice: false`) is the operator's choice, not a degradation.
Otherwise a completed run is still a degraded audit when its second voice is missing: `companion_voice.status` `failed`
or `fold_failed`, `counted_as` `duplicate_voice` or `sole_voice`, or `planned: false` WITH a `reason` (a companion that
never started: `no_workdir`, `no_route`, `prompt_copy_failed`) — set the `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker and name the
reason. On a host with no route to the other family at all (`no_route`: no key and no CLI for it) that marker is set on
every audit; `companion_voice: false` on the block is the operator's way to say one voice is the host's shape.

## Two voices and the rejected-payload contract (cycle-126 FR-2)

**Companion voice (D-2.1).** Every dissent plans a second chain from the *other* provider
family — the primary configured on the block decides: any primary outside the Anthropic family (OpenAI,
Google, xAI, unknown) gets the Anthropic chain (`opus` → `claude-headless`), an Anthropic-family primary gets the OpenAI chain
(`gpt-5.5` → `codex-headless`; KF-002 keeps `gpt-5.5-pro` out of the default). Credential *presence* (env → `.env.local` →
`.env`; the value is never read) decides only where the companion chain starts — with no key it
starts at the CLI hop. Both chains walk in parallel; the two completed envelopes are aggregated
(`verdict_quality.voices_succeeded_ids` lists only completed voices). `companion_voice.status` is `succeeded`,
`failed` or `fold_failed`; `verdict_quality.voices_planned` counts the aggregated envelopes — 2 whenever the companion ran,
completed or not (a failed one is listed in `voices_dropped`) — except a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's
succeeded voices: INV-5 lets it feed no envelope, so `voices_planned` stays 1 and `companion_voice` is its only record; a `duplicate_voice` companion contributes none, and a
dropped entry naming the model the companion answered with is removed (INV-5). `companion_voice.counted_as`
(`independent_voice`, `duplicate_voice`, `sole_voice` — the primary never answered) names the outcome, and `planned: false` with a `reason` (`no_workdir`, `no_route`,

companion's findings arrive re-numbered `DISS-C-NNN` with a `voice` field; the primary's carry

never blocking a review). Opt-out per block: `flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice: false`

`repair_attempted` / `repair_succeeded` whether the bounded repair round-trip ran.

this block are kept byte-identical (CMP-138 fails on any drift).

- **Two voices, one envelope.** The companion runs in its own sub-workdir with a log and its own copies of the prompt files.
  The envelope's `cost_usd` / tokens are BOTH voices; the per-voice spend stays under `companion_voice.cost_cents`, and

Output file: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`. The
`adversarial-review-gate.sh` hook checks that this file parses and carries `metadata.type` and `metadata.model` — a `--record-fallback` record names no model, so it never opens the gate: re-run the dissent (or the operator sets `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes). When `adversarial-audit.json` is ABSENT after the script exits — an aborted run leaves none: at start the script moves the previous round's envelope and sidecars aside as `.prev` and never restores them — record the failure with the script itself (a call this skill's allowlist holds; never a hand-written file):

```bash
.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --record-fallback failed --reason "<what happened>"
```

before proceeding. Branch on the `status` line the script prints on stdout, never on exit 2 alone (exit 2 with no status line is a usage error, or a standing envelope that stderr names):

- **An envelope stands after a run that took the run lock** — it is the script's own: triage it; never overwrite it.
- **`failed`** (no envelope: the run aborted) — the call above writes `{"findings": [], "metadata": {"status": "failed", "reason": "<what happened>", "rejected_summary": [], "rejected_sidecars": []}}` under the per-(sprint, gate) run lock. It never writes over an envelope that stands (exit 2), unless the run died before its lock with no status on stdout: what stands is then the previous round's — add `--since <the time on the run's "run started" stderr line>` and an envelope older than that goes aside as `.prev`.
- **`refused_concurrent_run`** (another run — a detached or backgrounded one — holds the run lock; nothing recorded, nothing moved; a `--record-fallback` made meanwhile is refused the same way) — wait until the holding run has exited: an envelope that then stands with a `metadata.timestamp` after your refusal is that run's: triage it as this round's dissent only when its `metadata.scope` is what you asked for (the same `diff_range` and `diff_oids` as your refusal's own `metadata.scope` — the commits, not just the ref names — and `run_tag` null: a chunk driver's tagged run reviewed one chunk); otherwise, or when none stands, run again.
- **`workdir_unavailable`, `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exceeded`, `diff_range_failed`** (the range's `git diff` failed — e.g. a base ref a shallow clone lacks; `workdir_unavailable` with `metadata.path` is a previous round's file that could not be moved aside — make the a2a directory writable; written BEFORE the run lock, or with it released; non-zero exit, stdout only; nothing moved aside, so any envelope at the path is the PREVIOUS run's and never this round's evidence) — record it: `--record-fallback <the status> --reason "<its stdout line>" --since <the run started time>` (it never displaces an envelope written after that) moves that envelope and its `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` sidecars aside as `<name>.prev` (as a run does at start) before it writes, so `verdict-derive.sh` judges this round's record, not the last round's.

A record names what it moved aside (`metadata.displaced`: status, timestamp, findings, rejected); `verdict-derive.sh` warns when that held findings. `verdict-derive.sh` never scans `.prev` files (they are the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback) and reports `.prev` files with NO envelope as a `dissent_aborted` violation, which a fallback record clears; `rejected_sidecars: []` does not silence a canonical `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` beside it — that is this run's own partial work, counted whether listed or not: triage its rows under `## Rejected dissent payloads`.

Then set a `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker in the audit report. Empty
findings from a run that completed are a normal pass, not a degraded review.

A bare `planned: false` (the block opted out, `companion_voice: false`) is the operator's choice, not a degradation.
Otherwise a completed run is still a degraded audit when its second voice is missing: `companion_voice.status` `failed`
or `fold_failed`, `counted_as` `duplicate_voice` or `sole_voice`, or `planned: false` WITH a `reason` (a companion that
never started: `no_workdir`, `no_route`, `prompt_copy_failed`) — set the `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker and name the
reason. On a host with no route to the other family at all (`no_route`: no key and no CLI for it) that marker is set on
every audit; `companion_voice: false` on the block is the operator's way to say one voice is the host's shape.

## Two voices and the rejected-payload contract (cycle-126 FR-2)

**Companion voice (D-2.1).** Every dissent plans a second chain from the *other* provider
family — the primary configured on the block decides: any primary outside the Anthropic family (OpenAI,
Google, xAI, unknown) gets the Anthropic chain (`opus` → `claude-headless`), an Anthropic-family primary gets the OpenAI chain
(`gpt-5.5` → `codex-headless`; KF-002 keeps `gpt-5.5-pro` out of the default). Credential *presence* (env → `.env.local` →
`.env`; the value is never read) decides only where the companion chain starts — with no key it
starts at the CLI hop. Both chains walk in parallel; the two completed envelopes are aggregated
(`verdict_quality.voices_succeeded_ids` lists only completed voices). `companion_voice.status` is `succeeded`,
`failed` or `fold_failed`; `verdict_quality.voices_planned` counts the aggregated envelopes — 2 whenever the companion ran,
completed or not (a failed one is listed in `voices_dropped`) — except a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's
succeeded voices: INV-5 lets it feed no envelope, so `voices_planned` stays 1 and `companion_voice` is its only record; a `duplicate_voice` companion contributes none, and a
dropped entry naming the model the companion answered with is removed (INV-5). `companion_voice.counted_as`
(`independent_voice`, `duplicate_voice`, `sole_voice` — the primary never answered) names the outcome, and `planned: false` with a `reason` (`no_workdir`, `no_route`,
`prompt_copy_failed`) is a companion that never started; a bare `planned: false` is the opt-out. The
companion's findings arrive re-numbered `DISS-C-NNN` with a `voice` field; the primary's carry
`voice` too. `metadata.companion_voice` records `{planned, family, family_basis, chain, model,
status: succeeded|failed|fold_failed, failure_class: auth|model_unavailable|quota|timeout|lock_wait|malformed|null,
cost_cents, attempts}`; a companion whose chain fails is a dropped voice (degraded for an audit,
never blocking a review). Opt-out per block: `flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice: false`
(the YAML boolean spellings in any case; a value that is none of them is reported and the voice stays on).

**Tolerant schema (D-2.2).** A finding missing only `failure_mode` is no longer dropped: the
first sentence of its `description` (≤ 200 chars) becomes `failure_mode` and the finding is
marked `failure_mode_derived: true` (a missing `id` is filled positionally, `id_derived: true`).
Severity, category and description are never touched. Payloads that still fail go to the
sidecar (`adversarial-rejected-<type>.jsonl`, `-companion` suffix for the second voice) **and**
to `metadata.rejected_summary[]` as `{index, severity, title, title_derived, anchor, reason, description_head}`.

**The contract (D-2.3).** When `rejected_summary` is non-empty the feedback file MUST contain a
`## Rejected dissent payloads` section with one line per entry — `- <title> (<severity>, <anchor>)
— <reason>: triaged as <real defect → counted under the matching heading | not a defect → why>`.
`verdict-derive.sh` reads the sibling envelope (`adversarial-<gate>.json`, or `--envelope <path>`)
and marks the trailer INCONSISTENT (exit 1) when the section is missing. Reading a sidecar row:
`payload` is the model's finding as normalised, `reject_reason` the clause it failed, and
`repair_attempted` / `repair_succeeded` whether the bounded repair round-trip ran.

**Round-1 hardening (sprint-248 review, sixteen live two-voice runs).** One list, by envelope field; both skills' copies of
this block are kept byte-identical (CMP-138 fails on any drift).

- **Two voices, one envelope.** The companion runs in its own sub-workdir with a log and its own copies of the prompt files.
  The envelope's `cost_usd` / tokens are BOTH voices; the per-voice spend stays under `companion_voice.cost_cents`, and
  `budget_cents` is a per-voice cap (a malformed cap is 0 cents — the run fails closed with `status: budget_exceeded`).
  Findings carry `voice` (the outer hop, matching `final_model`) and `answered_by` (the model that produced them);
  `companion_voice.answered_by` is the companion's own succeeded id. An operator may set
  `flatline_protocol.<block>.companion_chain: {anthropic: [...], openai: [...]}` to replace the default chains of D-2.1
  (used as given; only those two keys are read — keyed by the companion's family). A family with neither a credential nor its CLI on PATH is `reason: no_route`; a prompt copy that fails
  is `reason: prompt_copy_failed` (no fork). `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_KEEP_WORKDIR=1` keeps the `/tmp` workdir's files, never a
  process.
- **`companion_voice.independent` / `counted_as`.** Independence compares the two `answered_by` families (the primary's
  succeeded id, not its configured hop). Same family — or either family `unknown`, an id no catalog entry or name rule
  places, which is no evidence of a second family: the companion's findings are kept (tagged) but its envelope
  contributes no voice to verdict quality — `counted_as: duplicate_voice` (the aggregator counts distinct voices; its
  INV-5 forbids one id both succeeded and dropped, so a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's succeeded voices
  feeds no dropped-voice envelope either, and a MIXED attempt envelope keeps its own voice: a copy without the conflicting
  dropped entry is aggregated — `primary_attempts_rewritten` / `companion_attempts_rewritten`; an envelope with no
  succeeded voice that dropped the other side's voice is excluded — `primary_attempts_excluded` /
  `companion_attempts_excluded`). A primary that never answered leaves the companion `counted_as: sole_voice`
  (`independent: null`). A primary chain that exhausts while the companion completes is promoted (`status: reviewed`,
  `degraded: true`, `primary_voice: {status: failed}`) so the completed voice is never buried. An aggregator failure is
  named on the envelope (`verdict_quality_error`). A fold that fails keeps the primary envelope

- **Shared hops (`companion_voice.shared_hops`, `primary_voice.status: ceded`).** A hop both chains hold (typically the
  other family's CLI as the primary's last resort) stays in the companion chain and is listed under `shared_hops`,

DISS-C-001 [MEDIUM] voice=claude-headless secrets — An evaluated agent (or prompt-injected content it processes) runs `cat ~/.codex/auth.json` and exfiltrates a live OpenAI access token, identity token, or a non-expiring OPENAI_API_KEY over the container's network, giving an outside party use of the operator's OpenAI account/billing beyond the run.
   loc: ?
   make_home now rewrites the host's ~/.codex/auth.json into the per-run HOME, but it only redacts tokens.refresh_token. Every other key is copied verbatim: tokens.access_token, tokens.id_token (an identity JWT carrying the account's email/subject), tokens.account_id, and the top-level OPENAI_API_KEY when the host logged in with API-key auth. That file is mounted read-write at /home/evaluser inside the container where the evaluated agent runs arbitrary shell with network access. The new KF-048 pre-flight in run-ablation.sh additionally guarantees the access token is valid for at least 2 x summed watchdog / concurrency (hours), so an agent that reads the file always gets a live credential. OPENAI_API_KEY in particular does not expire. The test only asserts that the refresh token is replaced, so the long-lived key is never checked.
   fix: Allowlist instead of denylist: write only the keys the codex CLI needs for the chatgpt auth mode (auth_mode, tokens.access_token, tokens.account_id, placeholder refresh_token) and set OPENAI_API_KEY to null unless auth_mode is explicitly api-key; drop id_token if the CLI does not require it. Extend the KF-048 bats case to assert OPENAI_API_KEY is null in the copy. Longer term, mount auth.json read-only and only for phases that run the dissent.

DISS-C-002 [LOW] voice=claude-headless input-validation — A correct agent solution that adds a source module sharing a basename with a fixture test helper (common names: utils.py, helpers.py, conftest-adjacent fixtures) is mutilated before grading and recorded as a hidden-test failure, biasing arm comparisons.
   loc: ?
   The reserved-basename set is built from every .py file under any fixture directory whose path contains a component named tests or test (helpers.py, _oracle_x.py, utils.py, etc.), and it is then applied to the whole graded tree, not just test directories. pytest's default import-mode collision only concerns modules it actually collects/imports from package-less test dirs; a legitimately named production module such as src/pkg/utils.py or app/helpers.py does not collide, yet it is unlinked before the hidden suite runs. The grader thus deletes part of a correct solution and grades it as failing, which is the exact outcome 1.2.11 was meant to prevent. The deletion is silent to the agent (only grading/<label>.colliding-removed.txt records it).
   fix: Restrict the scan of the graded tree to paths that pytest will collect for the task's test_command (the tests/ or test/ roots, or directories matching the configured testpaths), and reserve only basenames pytest imports by name (test_*.py / *_test.py and sibling helpers inside the same rootdir), rather than any .py anywhere. Log removals into grade.json with paths so they are auditable per row.

DISS-C-003 [LOW] voice=claude-headless other — Tasks whose hidden suite is delivered as an overlay directory remain vulnerable to collection aborts (correct solution graded failing); vendored test trees cause spurious removals. Both skew grades silently.
   loc: ?
   reserved is derived only from overlay entries that are files (owned) and from the fixture tree. Overlay entries that are directories (owned_dirs) are excluded from the reservation: .py files inside a hidden overlay directory never enter reserved, so an agent file elsewhere in the tree with the same basename is not removed and the import-file-mismatch abort that 1.2.11 targets still occurs for those tasks. Conversely, the fixture walk's any(p in ('tests','test')) matches a component at any depth, so a vendored third-party test tree inside the fixture (e.g. vendor/lib/tests/test_core.py) reserves names against the agent's tree.
   fix: Walk each overlay directory (os.walk(full)) and add its .py basenames to reserved; anchor the fixture scan to the top-level tests/ or test/ roots the task's test_command actually runs rather than any path component.

def copy_tree(src, dst, top_exclude=frozenset()):
    """regular files, directories and in-tree relative symlinks only; caches dropped. A
    symlink whose target is absolute or resolves outside dst is not recreated (DISS-001).
    → the number of symlinks dropped"""
    os.makedirs(dst, exist_ok=True)
    dropped = 0
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(src, followlinks=False):
        rel = os.path.relpath(root, src)
        keep = []
        for d in sorted(dirs):
            if (rel == "." and d in top_exclude) or d in EXCLUDE_ANY:
                continue
            sp = os.path.join(root, d)
            dp = os.path.join(dst, rel, d)
            if os.path.islink(sp):
                target = os.readlink(sp)
                if link_escapes(target, rel):
                    dropped += 1
                else:
                    os.symlink(target, dp)
                continue
            os.makedirs(dp, exist_ok=True)
            keep.append(d)
        dirs[:] = keep
        for f in sorted(files):
            if rel == "." and f in top_exclude:
                continue
            sp, dp = os.path.join(root, f), os.path.join(dst, rel, f)
            st = os.lstat(sp)
            if stat.S_ISLNK(st.st_mode):
                target = os.readlink(sp)
                if link_escapes(target, rel):
                    dropped += 1
                else:
                    os.symlink(target, dp)
            elif stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
                if st.st_size > FILE_CAP:   # MEDIUM-A3: a sparse 1 TB file must not become a dense write
                    OVERSIZED[0] += 1
                    continue
                shutil.copyfile(sp, dp)
                os.chmod(dp, (st.st_mode & 0o777) | 0o600)
    return dropped + drop_escaping_links(dst)


def put_file(tree, rel, src):
    parts = safe_rel(rel)
    if parts is None:
        raise GradeError(f"unsafe path: {rel!r}")
    dst = ensure_parent(tree, parts)
    if os.path.lexists(dst):
        remove_path(dst)
    if os.path.isdir(src) and not os.path.islink(src):
        copy_tree(src, dst)
    else:
        shutil.copyfile(src, dst)
        os.chmod(dst, (os.stat(src).st_mode & 0o777) | 0o600)
